human_tolerance.notes: One of the most common birds across much of southeastern Brazil and the state bird of Sao Paulo since 1966; it walks on lawns and bare ground and perches in low trees to sing.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeds in the southern spring and summer; the cup nest is usually 4-5 m up in a tree, and incubation and fledging each take about 12-13 days.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Holds a territory and sings from a high perch.

vocalizations.description: A loud, liquid, fluting song of slow warbled phrases, given from a high perch in the tree canopy; famous in Brazil from the opening line of Cancao do Exilio.
A sharp, repeated tick or tlek call given when disturbed, sometimes followed by a harsh chattering.

taxonomy.note: GBIF Backbone Taxonomy gives Aves Passeriformes Turdidae and the authorship on the matched name; the Wikidata item confirms the English common name.

external.note: GBIF usage key 2490718 and iNaturalist taxon id 12738 as matched by the GBIF backbone and the iNaturalist taxa API; Wikidata Q609283 carries the same identifiers.

common_names.note: English common name from Wikidata; Portuguese name from the article's interlanguage links.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern for Rufous-bellied thrush.

range.note: Eastern and southeastern Brazil from Maranhao south to Rio Grande do Sul, plus Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay and central Argentina.

traits.body_plan.note: A perching passerine or parrot; biped_winged mesh.

traits.limb_count.note: Two legs; wings are not counted as limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Authored params for the shared perching-songbird program: a bolder flee distance than a robin because it flushes from open ground.

traits.metamorphosis.note: None; the young hatch as fledged nestlings.

traits.senses.note: Colour vision in all birds; hearing and olfaction values are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them here.

traits.nest_type.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; nest site from Wikipedia ('builds an open-cup nest'); the perch and shrub_thicket weights are judgement.

traits.mass_kg.note: AVONET Mass 69.44 g; Wikipedia gives about 59 g for males and 64 g for females as usual weights, up to 68 g and 78 g. 0.064 kg is the usual female weight.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia: 'can reach a length of 25 cm'.

traits.social.note: Territorial, in pairs outside the breeding season; group_size [1, 2] is judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal 0 (diurnal); Rufous-bellied thrush describes daytime activity.

traits.defense.note: Authored: flies to cover when disturbed.

traits.wariness.note: Authored. Wary of people but common in city gardens, so set low; not a measured flight distance.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: roosts in dense vegetation or a cavity.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; nest site from Wikipedia ('builds an open-cup nest'); the perch and shrub_thicket weights are judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia: one of the most common birds across much of southeastern Brazil, known as sabia-laranjeira, and the state bird of Sao Paulo since 1966.

seasonal.strategy.note: A year-round resident of subtropical Brazil with no migration or dormancy described.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding window and the 12-13 day incubation and fledging from Wikipedia; the end of the breeding window and the territorial phase are judgements.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg and nest timing from Wikipedia; Juvenile duration and scale are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored params for the shared perching-songbird program: a bolder flee distance than a robin because it flushes from open ground.

look.note: Colours from the Wikipedia description (grey-brown head and upperparts, bright rufous-orange belly and flanks, dark malar stripe, pale throat, dark bill); proportions authored for a thrush.

traits.wingspan_m.note: AVONET Wing.Length 115.5 mm is the wing chord, not the spread; multiplied by 2.80, the ratio this repository's own sourced thrush record (species/turdus-merula: 0.36 m over an AVONET chord of 128.4 mm) gives for thrushes. Authored conversion, not a measured wingspan.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: AVONET Mass 69.44 g; Wikipedia gives about 59 g for males and 64 g for females as usual weights, up to 68 g and 78 g. 0.064 kg is the usual female weight.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No openly licensed source states a wild lifespan for this species. Authored as a low-precision value typical of a thrush of this size; it is a judgement, not a measurement, and should be replaced if a licensed source is found.

vocalizations.song.note: Call description from the Rufous-bellied thrush article; months, time windows, cooldowns and loudness are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them.
